newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 21.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- President Kim Young-sam plans to invite leaders of the three main political parties to the presidential Blue House today to discuss strike-related issues.
- Tempartures in Seoul are forecast to plunge below minus 10 degrees celcius today, while the rest of the nation is expected to face strong winds with heavy snow near the eastern coast.

- Park Seong-yawng, former chairman of the Kumho group and vice chairman of the Federation of Korean Industries, has been appointed to head a 31-member presidential panel to introduce major financial reform.
- The North Korean military is producing and smuggling opium, while its government is locating relatives in the country on behalf of overseas Koreans for a fee, defector Kim Kyung-ho said.
- A real estate tax will be reintroduced after being discarded in 1993. The tax will be levied on regions where land prices have jumped more than 15 percent each year.

- From April 1 the Fair Trade Commission will sharply ease reporting rules concerning business consolidation, by applying it only to firms with asset value or annual sales above 100 billion won, instead of 20 billion won. Also, subsidiaries possessing under ten percent of unlisted sister company shares as opposed to three percent in the past, will be able gain recognition as an independent company or group.
